title: Ex7 - Open: Hue interpretation
text:
Run the code below in a new cell:

```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

url = 'https://github.com/muratfirat78/CPP_Datasets/raw/main/auto.xlsx'
dfAuto = pd.read_excel(url)
dfAuto['acceleration'] = dfAuto['acceleration']/10
dfAuto = dfAuto.drop(dfAuto.loc[dfAuto['acceleration'] == 95].index)

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16,10))
ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
colors = {'USA': 'blue', 'Japan': 'red', 'Germany': 'green'}
ax.scatter(dfAuto['acceleration'], dfAuto['mpg'], s=400,
           c=dfAuto['origin'].apply(lambda x: colors[x]), alpha=0.3, edgecolors='black')
plt.title('MPG vs. Acceleration')
plt.xlabel('Acceleration')
plt.ylabel('MPG')
plt.show()
```

In the scatter plot colored by country of origin (USA=blue, Japan=red, Germany=green): which country's cars tend to have the highest mpg? What does this suggest about design priorities?
answer: Japanese cars (red) cluster at higher mpg values. USA cars (blue) tend to have lower mpg and higher acceleration. This suggests Japanese manufacturers prioritized fuel efficiency.
